****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] says that it mistakenly [[Killing of Alon Shamriz, Yotam Haim, and Samer Talalka|shot dead]] three [[hostage]]s in [[friendly fire]] incidents in the [[Shuja'iyya]] neighborhood of [[Gaza City]]. **[[Yemeni Crisis (2011–present)|Yemeni Crisis]]
***[[Red Sea crisis]]
****Two [[Liberia]]n-flagged vessels in the [[Bab-el-Mandeb]] strait are attacked with [[drone warfare|drone]]s and [[ballistic missile]]s launched by [[Houthi movement|Houthi]] militants in [[Yemen]], causing a fire on one of the ships. '''Arts and culture'''
*[[Albania]] returns 20 [[icon]]s to [[North Macedonia]] that were [[Smuggling|trafficked]] a decade ago, according to [[Ministry of Culture (Albania)|Albania's Culture Ministry]]. A handover ceremony is held at the [[National History Museum (Albania)|National History Museum]] in the Albanian capital, [[Tirana]]. [https://apnews.com/article/albania-north-macedonia-stolen-icons-d546e4da91f05c6dd891754acc62a5b4 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[President of Mexico|President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] [[inaugurate]]s the first part of the [[Tourism in Mexico|tourist]] [[Maya Train]], that runs in a rough loop around the [[Yucatán Peninsula]]. The [[United States dollar|$]]20 billion, 950-mile line will connect [[beach resort]]s and [[archaeological site]]s. [https://apnews.com/article/mexico-maya-train-tourist-rail-yucatan-81d827ff51589fe43ed608ffb309be4a (AP)]
*The [[International Energy Agency]] forecasts that global [[coal]] consumption is expected to reach a record high this year, as demand in emerging and [[developing economies]] remains strong. The demand for coal is predicted to increase by 1.4 percent this year, surpassing 8.5 billion tonnes for the first time. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/12/15/global-coal-use-to-reach-record-high-in-2023-iea (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[English Channel migrant crossings (2018–present)|English Channel migrant crossings]]
**One person is killed and another is hospitalized after a boat carrying more than 60 [[Illegal immigration to the United Kingdom|migrants]] experienced difficulties as it attempted to cross the [[English Channel]] from [[France]] to the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://apnews.com/article/france-britain-migrants-channel-efa66b943128594ebe3069142075123f (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Gaza humanitarian crisis|2023 Gaza humanitarian crisis]], [[Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
**[[Israel]] authorizes the temporary use of its [[Kerem Shalom border crossing]] to deliver [[International aid to Palestinians|humanitarian aid]] to the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2023/12/991039/israel-says-allows-temporary-entry-aid-gaza-through-new-border (AFP via ''NST'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Nigerien crisis]]
**An [[ECOWAS]] court orders former [[President of Niger|President]] [[Mohamed Bazoum]] to be freed from arrest and reinstated as president. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/west-african-court-orders-nigers-president-released-reinstated-105688607 (AP via ABC News)]
*[[Indigenous peoples in Guatemala]]
**A ruling from the [[Inter-American Court of Human Rights]] finds [[Guatemala]] to have violated [[indigenous rights]] by allowing a large [[nickel mine]] to operate on tribal land. [https://apnews.com/article/guatemala-mine-indigenous-rights-court-nickel-fenix-346b0c882d4ee52954a7bd32c81202a5 (AP)]
*[[Keretsky grenade incident]]
**A [[councillor]] detonates three [[grenade]]s at a meeting of the village council of Keretsky, [[Zakarpattia Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], injuring 27 people, including himself. [https://www.barrons.com/news/ukrainian-councillor-throws-grenades-at-meeting-wounding-26-b3c4d353 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[News of the World royal phone hacking scandal]]
**[[Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex]] wins a [[phone hacking]] lawsuit against the publisher of the ''[[Daily Mirror]]'' in the first of several lawsuits against British [[tabloid journalism|tabloids]] to go to trial. The [[High Court of Justice|High Court]] found that phone hacking was widespread at the [[Mirror Group]] and that [[private investigators]] gathered information unlawfully. [https://apnews.com/article/prince-harry-phone-hacking-lawsuit-ruling-daily-mirror-cb19ead248b085ed388219b27d5b66bd (AP)]
*[[Post-election lawsuits related to the 2020 U.S. presidential election]]
**A [[Juries in the United States#Federal jury|United States federal jury]] orders [[Rudy Giuliani]], former lawyer for former [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], to pay [[United States dollar|$]]148 million in [[damages]] for [[United States defamation law|defaming]] two [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgian]] [[election official]]s with false [[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election|electoral fraud]] claims about the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 U.S. presidential election]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231215-ex-trump-lawyer-giuliani-ordered-to-pay-148-mn-for-defaming-poll-workers (AFP via France 24)]
*Fourteen workers at the [[Tenerife South Airport]] in [[Tenerife]], [[Canary Islands]], [[Spain]], are arrested on suspicion of stealing items from checked-in luggage. Police seize allegedly stolen items worth almost [[Euro|€]]2 million. [https://apnews.com/article/spain-airport-luggage-thefts-tenerife-canary-islands-58ab9f658db9ba9552341b64d03bc085 (AP)]
*State [[prosecutor]]s in [[Thailand]] indict a member of the country’s [[Senate of Thailand|Senate]], [[Upakit Pachariyangkun]], on six charges involving [[narcotics trafficking]], [[money laundering]] and association with a transnational [[criminal organization]]. [https://apnews.com/article/thailand-money-launder-drug-trafficking-senator-myanmar-d6e9588c1f63b5b68bb1167d6d81655e (AP)]
*[[Chile]]'s [[Carabineros de Chile|police]] arrest at least 55 people in one of the country's largest [[fiscal fraud]] cases, amounting to about $275 million and implicating small- and mid-sized companies in different parts of the country. The suspects will stand trial for tax crimes, criminal association, [[money laundering]], customs fraud and making false declarations. [https://apnews.com/article/chile-fiscal-fraud-arrests-tax-52f1b7fefbdcf6f68d959915cfba0944 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Corruption in Belgium]], [[Chinese intelligence activity abroad]]
**A joint investigation by the ''[[Financial Times]]'', ''[[Der Spiegel]]'', and ''[[Le Monde]]'' reveals that Belgian [[Vlaams Belang]] politician [[Frank Creyelman]] accepted [[bribes]] from the [[Ministry of State Security (China)|Chinese Ministry of State Security]] for three years in order to influence discussions within the [[European Union]]. Creyelman was subsequently expelled from the party. [https://www.ft.com/content/601df41f-8393-46ad-9f74-fe64f8ea1a3f (''Financial Times'')]
